method: Core commitments: statements on which the coded profiles of an ideology's mainstream all take the same side. They are AI coders' judgements, checked for counterexamples but not with adherents or experts, so they do not establish what every adherent holds. Three Opus coders (lenses: theorist, insider, sceptic) proposed commitments independently; an entry is kept when at least 2 of 3 proposed it (coders = how many), and each was checked against the ideology's coded answer sheet (required side at |v| >= 2 in every required frame). side is the sign of the raw answer (+1 agree, -1 disagree) to the statement as worded; the item key is not applied. frame I checks the ideal-system answer; both also checks here and now. A decisive contradiction (|answer| >= 2 on the wrong side) rules the ideology out. Entries whose adherents simulated from the coded sheets are ruled out more than 2% of the time (a consistency check against our own coding, not against real adherents) are moved to dropped by scripts/commitments-audit.ts. Entries refuted by a counterexample (sincere mainstream adherents who reject the statement on principle) are moved to dropped by hand, with the reason. Content v2 (2026-10-31) added red-line commitments (kind "red-line", on the off-axis red-line statements; they rule an ideology out exactly like core ones and do not count toward the core cap of 6) and core commitments on the new Full statements, coded by the same three lenses under the same 2-of-3 and coded-sheet rules (scripts/merge-commitments.ts). Raw coder output: commitments-raw.json (v1 under batches, v2 under v2).

Secular law guided by reason and science, not religious authority, is the core of laiklik.
Citizenship is civic and shared; the republic does not jail innocent people for their ancestry.
Laiklik keeps religion out of law and politics while guaranteeing each citizen's freedom of conscience.
Modern, secular law makes guilt personal; punishing relatives belongs to the old order the reforms replaced.
Sovereignty belongs to the nation and the republic replaced the sultan; no ruler stands above the law.

peronism.why: Political sovereignty and economic independence, two of Peronism's three banners, put the nation's own people first in loyalty.
Peronist social justice and state-directed development require the state to shape production, not leave it to prices and competition alone.
Immigrants of every origin built the nation and share one national-popular identity; jailing people for their ethnicity betrays that.
We respect the Catholic tradition and the people's faith; no one should be punished by the state for their religion.
Social justice punishes no one for a relative's crime.
Our movement rests on the people's vote; we were banned from elections ourselves and know cancelling them silences the workers.

classical-liberalism.why: Private property is a natural right in classical liberalism, so common ownership of nearly all productive assets contradicts it.
Classical liberalism requires government by consent with power limited and checked, which rules out permanent single-party rule.
Classical liberalism holds that markets and voluntary exchange, not planners, should coordinate the economy.
Government exists to secure rights by keeping order and enforcing law through courts and police; limited, not abolished.
Every individual has rights to life and liberty; imprisoning the innocent because of ethnicity is a gross violation.
Church and state are separate, with full religious toleration for every faith and none.
The state exists to secure rights; torturing a suspect is the very abuse of power constitutions exist to prevent.
Habeas corpus is a foundational protection against arbitrary detention by government.
Rights and guilt belong to individuals; punishing innocent relatives violates their natural rights.
Free speech is a core liberty; peaceful criticism of government must never be punished.
Government rests on the consent of the governed; cancelling elections to keep power removes the check that consent provides.
The rule of law means government is bound by general rules that apply equally to rulers and ruled.
Even in a just war, innocent people keep their rights; deliberately killing civilians can never be justified by winning.
Rights protect everyone, including political opponents; force is only for defending rights against actual aggression.

minarchism.why: Minarchism holds property fully private, so common ownership of nearly all productive assets contradicts it.
The minimal state is limited to police, courts and defence, so it cannot redistribute wealth from rich to poor.
Under self-ownership and non-aggression, punishing a person for conduct that harms only themselves is illegitimate force.
A night-watchman state has no role in planning production, which minarchists leave entirely to markets.
Beyond police, courts and defence, schooling, health and welfare belong to markets, charity and voluntary associations, not taxation.
The legitimate state is a minimal one that provides police, courts and defence to protect rights.
Imprisoning people who have harmed no one is initiating force, the core wrong a legitimate state exists to stop.
Church and state are separate, and the state has no business punishing anyone's beliefs.
Courts exist to protect individuals' rights, above all against being held by the state without justification.
Each person owns themselves and answers only for their own actions; punishing family members is aggression against the innocent.
Peaceful speech harms no one's rights, so jailing someone for it is an act of aggression.
Rulers have no right to keep power by cancelling votes; that is using state force to protect themselves, not people's rights.
The rule against initiating force applies to everyone, including those running the state.
Force is only legitimate against those who initiate force; disagreeing politically is not aggression.

georgism.why: Free trade is a core Georgist commitment, set out in George's own 'Protection or Free Trade'.
Georgism wants taxes on trade replaced by a land-value tax, so tariffs favouring local goods contradict it.
Beyond collecting land rent, Georgism leaves the economy to markets and private enterprise, not central planning.
Civil liberties and equal rights to the earth belong to everyone; jailing the innocent for their ethnicity violates both.
We are secular and treat belief as a private matter, so no one should be punished for their religion.
Civil liberties require that anyone the state detains can challenge it before an independent court.
People own what they do; guilt, like earnings, belongs to the individual, not their family.
Civil liberties include criticising government freely; jailing peaceful critics is never acceptable.
We support democracy; the community whose land rents fund government must keep the power to choose it.
Ending privilege is our cause; no one, least of all rulers, should stand above the law.
We are internationalist and peaceful; deliberately killing civilians can never be justified.
We support democracy and peaceful reform; violence against political opponents is never acceptable.

paleolibertarianism.why: Paleolibertarians treat property rights as absolute and private, so common ownership of nearly all productive assets contradicts it.
Decentralisation, states' rights and secession are central to paleolibertarianism, which sees small units as the safeguard of liberty.
Paleolibertarianism rejects global governance and supranational institutions as the extreme form of the centralised state it opposes.
Welfare and public schooling destroy families and communities; markets, churches and charity should provide.
The state imprisoning people who have harmed no one is exactly the central-state aggression we oppose.
Christianity is upheld by private communities and covenants, never by state punishment of belief.
We oppose expanding state security powers; torture is the most extreme form of them.
Anyone the state detains must be able to challenge it; unchecked detention is state power at its most dangerous.
Property and justice are individual; punishing a criminal's innocent family is aggression against people who did nothing.
Opposing the central state is our cause; jailing peaceful critics is the state silencing its opponents.
The state is the great enemy of liberty; its rulers must never be exempt from the rules that bind everyone else.
We are strongly anti-war; deliberately killing civilians is mass murder by the state, whatever the war aims.

anarcho-communism.why: Anarcho-communism holds that everything belongs to everyone, with production held in common by communes and workers' associations.
Abolishing capital and private ownership of the means of production is a defining anarcho-communist aim.
Anarcho-communists reject any ruling party or 'workers' state' as a new set of rulers.
It replaces markets and money with distribution by need, so letting prices and competition alone decide production contradicts it.
The state must be abolished, not captured; a monopoly on force just creates rulers.
Society should be organised from below by free communes and associations, with no state.
Humanity is one, without borders or nations; jailing people for their ethnicity is domination in its purest form.
Religion is a private matter; no authority may punish anyone for their beliefs.
Torture is coercive authority at its cruellest, the opposite of a free society of mutual aid.
We oppose prisons and state detention; anyone the state holds must at least be able to challenge it.
Punishing whole families is authority at its most unjust; we reject hierarchical punishment altogether.
Jailing critics is the state protecting its rulers, the very authority we oppose.
We oppose militarism and the wars of states; deliberately killing civilians is the crime of rulers against peoples.

anarcho-syndicalism.why: In the syndicalist ideal, workers' collectives hold the means of production in common.
Anarcho-syndicalism's programme is for workers to take over the means of production and run them through their syndicates.
It seeks to expropriate capital, so wanting productive assets privately owned by investors contradicts it.
Anarcho-syndicalism rejects all parties and the state, so permanent single-party rule contradicts it.
No party, no parliament, no state: free association and the organised workers replace police power.
Society should be run by federated workers' syndicates and assemblies, with no state.
Workers of all countries and origins share one cause; jailing people for their ethnicity divides and oppresses them.
Religion is a private matter; no authority should punish anyone for their beliefs.
Torture is state coercion at its worst, the opposite of free association.
We oppose state detention of workers and activists; anyone held must be able to challenge it.
Punishing a whole family for one person's act is the arbitrary authority workers organise to abolish.
Jailing critics is how states crush workers' movements; peaceful dissent must never be punished.
We oppose militarism; deliberately killing civilians makes working people pay for their rulers' wars.

mutualism.why: Mutualism rejects absentee ownership that collects profit without working, which is exactly what passive shareholding is.
Mutualists want authority dissolved into contract and voluntary federation, which rules out single-party rule.
Mutualism is market anarchism: it holds that markets, not planning, should coordinate production.
Authority should dissolve into contracts and voluntary federation; no body should monopolise force.
Order should come from contracts and voluntary federation among communes and associations, not a state.
Newcomers are welcome as equals and we oppose national borders; imprisoning people for ethnicity is pure domination.
Religion is a private matter, never something authority should punish.
Liberty is central and authority should dissolve into contract; torture is coercion at its most extreme.
Liberty requires that anyone the state detains can challenge it before an independent court.
Justice is reciprocity between individuals; punishing a family for one member's act is no justice at all.
Liberty is central; jailing peaceful critics is authority protecting itself.
We are anti-militarist; deliberately killing civilians can never be justified.

libertarian-municipalism.why: Libertarian municipalism calls for land and enterprises to be municipalised, owned in common by the community.
The doctrine rejects private ownership of the economy in favour of control by citizen assemblies.
Libertarian municipalism puts policy-making in face-to-face assemblies, which permanent rule by one party would replace.
Bookchin's confederalism gives wider councils only the coordinating powers that municipal assemblies delegate to them.
The nation-state, with its professional police and monopoly of force, should be replaced by a confederation of citizen assemblies.
Newcomers become equal citizens of the assembly; jailing people for their ethnicity is the opposite.
We are secular and rational; belief is free, and no authority should punish anyone for it.
Security comes from a self-governing community, not police power; torture is domination at its worst.
Civic freedom requires that no one can be held by the state without challenge before an independent court.
Free citizens answer for their own acts; collective family punishment is domination, not justice.
Open public debate is the heart of assembly democracy; peaceful criticism must never be punished.
Politics belongs to citizens deciding together; cancelling a vote because of its likely result destroys self-government.
We oppose rule by a separate political class; where rulers exist, they must be bound by the same law.
We are anti-militarist; militias only defend communities, and deliberately killing civilians is never acceptable.

anarcho-capitalism.why: Common ownership of productive assets is incompatible with the absolute private property anarcho-capitalism rests on.
Anarcho-capitalism holds that all property is private, including every productive asset.
Because taxation is held to be theft, wealth gained through voluntary exchange belongs entirely to the person who earned it.
Anarcho-capitalists hold that free markets should coordinate everything, with no planning authority.
A territorial monopoly on force funded by taxation is illegitimate; law, courts and defence can be supplied by competing firms.
Law, courts and policing should be provided by competing private agencies and voluntary contracts, with no state.
Imprisoning people who have harmed no one is aggression, the core wrong of the non-aggression principle.
There is no state religion and no state moral code; punishing belief is aggression.
Torturing a suspect is aggression against a person who may be innocent, the worst kind of state power.
Anyone the state holds must be able to challenge it; detention is force that has to be justified.
No one may initiate force against the innocent; punishing family members for another's crime is aggression.
Peaceful speech harms no one; jailing someone for it is aggression.
No one has special rights to use force, including those who claim to rule.
Deliberately killing civilians is aggression against innocents; war aims cannot justify it.

anarcho-primitivism.why: Anarcho-primitivism rejects the state and all rulers, so long-term single-party rule contradicts it.
Anarcho-primitivists explicitly oppose genetic engineering, still more so for enhancement.
Anarcho-primitivism rejects technology as a system and explicitly opposes AI development.
The tradition opposes life extension as part of the technological project it wants dismantled.
Small, face-to-face bands decide informally, with no state, police or rulers.
There are no nations or borders in our ideal; jailing people for their ethnicity is state domination at its worst.
We see organised religion as domination, but punishing people's beliefs is domination too.
Torture is the state's domination of the body, part of the civilisation we oppose.
We oppose state captivity; anyone the state holds must at least be able to challenge it.
Punishing families is the domination civilisation brought; egalitarian bands have no rulers to impose it.
Jailing peaceful critics is the state protecting its rulers, which we oppose.

absolute-monarchism.why: Under absolute monarchy the ruler is chosen by hereditary succession, not by a popular vote of adults.
Parties competing to replace those in power contradict a sovereign who is not answerable to elections or parliaments.
A reigning dynasty being replaceable by voters is incompatible with hereditary, unaccountable-to-voters sovereignty.
Absolute monarchism is defined by undivided sovereign power vested in a hereditary monarch.
Hereditary succession puts a ruler raised for the role, above faction and with clear succession, at the head of the realm.
The sovereign is bound by divine and natural law and conscience, but not by the laws he himself makes for his subjects.

constitutional-monarchism.why: A monarch above party politics presupposes competing parties in parliament, which permanent single-party rule would abolish.
Constitutional monarchism holds that the monarch reigns but does not rule, with government accountable to parliament, so one leader acting without lawmakers' approval contradicts it.
A hereditary head of state stands above party politics and embodies the nation's continuity, which an elected one cannot.
All subjects or citizens stand equal under one crown; jailing innocent people for ethnicity violates the rule of law.
Whether or not a realm keeps an established church, every subject is free to follow any faith or none.
Habeas corpus is part of the constitutional heritage the crown embodies and protects.
Liberal democracy under the rule of law punishes individuals for their own crimes, never their families.
Liberal democracy and civil liberties mean criticising the government peacefully must never be a crime.
Governing power belongs to an elected parliament; the crown guards the constitution, including the voters' right to change government.
Armed forces loyal to the crown fight under the law of war; deliberately killing civilians is a war crime.
The monarchy stands above party conflict so that politics stays peaceful; violence against opponents is never acceptable.

technocracy.why: Technocracy is defined by giving qualified experts, not voters, control over technical policy decisions.
Technocratic governance is secular and evidence-based, so giving religious leaders a formal law-making role contradicts it.
Jailing law-abiding people by ethnicity is irrational prejudice, the opposite of evidence-based government.
The state is strictly secular; belief is private and no one should be punished for it.
Rational, evidence-based justice targets the person responsible; punishing relatives is arbitrary and achieves nothing measurable.
Competent, rational order requires rules that bind decision-makers as much as everyone else.
Problems are solved by expertise and evidence, not by violence against political opponents.

confucian-meritocracy.why: Confucian meritocracy holds that governing requires virtue and competence, so officials selected by merit rather than popular opinion should decide.
Benevolent government exists for the people's welfare; imprisoning innocent people for their ethnicity is cruel and unjust rule.
Mencius praised the sage king who did not punish a criminal's wife and children; benevolent rule punishes only the guilty.
Mencius condemned rulers who kill people to win wars; benevolent government wins by moral influence, not slaughter of civilians.

developmental-authoritarianism.why: Developmental authoritarianism has the state guide industrial priorities rather than letting prices and competition alone decide output.
The developmental state is defined by steering investment and credit toward national development goals.
Leaving investment to pure returns is the unguided market allocation that developmental states reject in favour of industrial policy.
Ethnic groups are managed for harmony under a shared national identity; jailing innocent people for ethnicity destroys that harmony.

neoreaction.why: Neoreaction rejects democracy and wants citizens treated as customers with exit, not as voters who choose the government.
Neocameralism gives a sovereign CEO secure power, which party competition to replace the government contradicts.
Neoreaction's ideal is a patchwork of many competing small sovereigns, the opposite of a binding world government.

transhumanism.why: Transhumanists favour genetic therapy and morphological freedom, so a blanket ban on heritable editing for any purpose contradicts them.
Overcoming ageing through life extension is a founding goal of transhumanism.
Transhumanism rejects 'natural' limits and treats ageing as a condition medicine should defeat.
Morphological freedom and brain-computer interfaces are core transhumanist aims, so opposing safe brain-computer links for healthy people contradicts them.
We welcome diversity and extend rights ever wider; jailing people for ethnicity is the opposite.
The state is secular and freedom of mind is central; no one should be punished for belief.
We defend civil liberties and bodily autonomy; torture is the gravest violation of both.
Civil liberties require that anyone detained by the state can challenge it before an independent court.
Each person is responsible for their own choices; punishing relatives violates individual rights.
Civil liberties include free criticism of government; jailing peaceful critics is never acceptable.
We rely on liberal democracy to keep technology fair; cancelling elections destroys the institutions that make that possible.
Democratic institutions only protect people when those in power are bound by the same law.
Our goal is reducing suffering and death; deliberately killing civilians is never acceptable.
We are liberal democrats and dovish; violence against political opponents is never acceptable.

critical-rationalism.why: That is what democracy is for: removing bad laws and bad leaders without bloodshed.
The key question is not who should rule but how to limit and remove bad rulers peacefully.
Piecemeal, reversible reforms let us learn from mistakes; complete redesigns cannot.
Laws must be open to criticism; revelation or authority placed beyond dispute blocks error correction.
Utopian redesigns to a plan concentrate power, cannot learn from mistakes and end in violence.
We are individualists; imprisoning innocent people for their ethnicity is tribalism at its worst.
Church and state are separate, and the open society tolerates all beliefs, including none.
Institutions must limit the harm rulers can do; licensing torture hands officials exactly the unchecked power we fear.
Independent courts check the state's power over individuals; detention without challenge cannot be corrected.
The open society holds individuals responsible for their own acts; collective family punishment is tribal, not civilised.
Criticism is how we find our mistakes; jailing peaceful critics shuts down error correction.
Democracy exists so bad governments can be removed peacefully; cancelling elections destroys the one mechanism that corrects rulers.
The rule of law must bind rulers like everyone else, or bad rulers cannot be checked.
Force is for stopping aggression and defending open societies, never for deliberately killing civilians.
The open society settles disputes by argument and votes; violence against opponents is what its enemies do.

dropped.reason: Refuted by counterexample, not by noise: militant democracy (e.g. Germany's Basic Law Art. 21(2), party bans supported by mainstream CDU and SPD figures) sincerely rejects "any group" being free to run, so must-agree falsely rules such adherents out of the whole democratic mainstream at once. The item's universal "any" is a quantifier beyond the core belief (CF review D2/B4/D3).
